Claim tested: ahk1 has three TM helices at 277-297, 374-394, 400-420
Key finding: Three TM features, all ECO:0000255 (automated sequence analysis), no named source method; these features are the sole basis of the Membrane keyword

Citation: QuickGO / PomBase annotation record for SPAC7D4.03c
Claim tested: ahk1 is located in a membrane
Key finding: PomBase assigns GO:0005575 cellular_component with ECO:0000307 (ND, no biological data available), GO_REF:0000015, on the same gene that carries IEA GO:0016020 located_in membrane (ECO:0007322, GO_REF:0000044)
Context: S. pombe, manual curation vs automatic pipeline
Confidence and limitations: Database-level, but a direct internal conflict: curators recorded no localization data.

Claim tested: the 3-TM topology is reproducible by an independent predictor
Key finding: Phobius reproduces 3 TM for O14260 (o272-293i376-394o400-422i), within 5 residues of UniProt; so the call is a genuine property of this sequence, not a database error
Confidence and limitations: Strong as a prediction-level result. Phobius and the UniProt pipeline share HMM assumptions, so this is not fully independent.

Claim tested: the three helices are conserved membrane-spanning helices
Key finding: 0 TM and 0 SP in all eight orthologs: S9W252 (S. cryophilus), Q07454 (S. cerevisiae Ahk1), A0A1G4K421, A0A1G4KJW1, A0A8J2T9L5, G8JRH5, J8Q6X5, Q6FWF2
Confidence and limitations: Strong. A 3-pass topology that no ortholog shares is not a conserved architecture.

Citation: Pfam PF08578 / InterPro IPR013887 member sampling + Phobius
Claim tested: the 3-TM topology is a family feature
Key finding: Of a random 60-member PF08578 sample, 53 returned predictions: 48/53 (90.6%) 0 TM, 4/53 1 TM, 1/53 (1.9%) 3 TM, and that one is O14260
Confidence and limitations: Strong. ahk1 is the singular outlier in its own domain family.

Citation: AlphaFold DB AF-O14260-F1 v6 + Shrake-Rupley SASA (this work)
Claim tested: the segments present a lipid-facing surface
Key finding: Mean RSA 0.083 +- 0.059 across the three segments, more buried than 18 genuine TM helices from six S. pombe polytopic plasma-membrane proteins (0.213 +- 0.079; U=6, p=0.017, rank-biserial 0.78) and than 18 soluble hydrophobic cores (0.279 +- 0.179; U=2, p=0.006). Only 8 of 63 segment residues have RSA > 0.25
Context: Single-chain AlphaFold models, matched S. pombe controls
Confidence and limitations: Moderate to strong. n=3 segments. Burial in a single-chain model is the expected signature of a protein core, and a real TM helix retains an exposed lipid face.

Citation: AlphaFold AF-O14260-F1 v6, helix-axis SVD (this work)
Claim tested: the three helices form a membrane-spanning bundle
Key finding: Pairwise axis angles 76, 110 and 158 deg; mean 56.1 deg versus 24.8 +- 13.9 deg for six polytopic membrane controls (z = +2.26) and 62.0 +- 12.1 deg for six soluble controls (z = -0.48). Segment 277-297 spans 20.1 A end-to-end over 21 residues, short of the ~30 A needed to cross a bilayer
Confidence and limitations: Moderate. Geometry is model-derived; AlphaFold packs membrane proteins without a bilayer, which can distort tilt.

Claim tested: the segments can be inserted by Sec61
Key finding: Apparent insertion free energies +1.49, +3.35 and +2.16 kcal/mol, all unfavourable, against -3.01 (pma1 TM3) and -1.48 (trk1 TM3) for real TM helices
Confidence and limitations: Moderate. pkd2 TM2 (Q09917 197-217) is a real TM helix that also scores +3.40, so positive dG alone does not exclude insertion.

Citation: Needleman-Wunsch O14260 vs S9W252 + AlphaFold models (this work)
Claim tested: hydrophobicity of the segments is under selection as a membrane anchor
Key finding: 45.8% global identity; the three segments align 1:1 at 76/62/67% identity (above background) with matched burial (RSA 0.067/0.132/0.059) and pLDDT, but charged-residue count doubles (3 to 6 DEKR) and segment 1 goes FCASILVLSFFQLPLFADHFL to FCAKILVLSFFKLENFAKHFL (3 Lys gained), dG +4.56 kcal/mol
Confidence and limitations: Strong. Position and burial are conserved while membrane-insertion competence is not, which is the signature of a core, not an anchor.

Claim tested: S. cerevisiae Ahk1 lacks equivalent segments
Key finding: Q07454 has its own equally buried hydrophobic segment (123-143 ELTSVCLECLSKIMTILIILP, mean RSA 0.053, 90% buried, peak KD19 1.98, exceeding every ahk1 segment) and carries no TM annotation; SGD also assigns ND
Confidence and limitations: Moderate. Shows buried hydrophobic stretches of this kind are normal and are not annotated as TM elsewhere.

Claim tested: Ahk1 is a cytoplasmic MAPK scaffold
Key finding: S. cerevisiae Ahk1 is described as a scaffold for the Sln1-branch Hog1 osmostress pathway; this is the source of the PomBase ISO transfer to ahk1 (GO:0005078, GO:0000165)
Confidence and limitations: Primary but heterologous. The orthology premise itself is weak: O14260 vs Q07454 is 181/777 = 23.3% identity with a negative global score, different OrthoDB/eggNOG/HOGENOM groups.

Claim tested: ahk1 localizes to a membrane in vivo
Key finding: Matsuyama et al. YFP-tagged 4,431 S. pombe proteins (~90% of the proteome), but the SPAC7D4.03c result could not be retrieved programmatically; PomBase's GO:0005575 ND annotation implies no localization data is held for this gene
Confidence and limitations: Unresolved. This is the single most decisive missing datum and it may well exist in the published dataset.
